children: Genesys International Corporation has won a Rs 283 crore World Bank-funded contract to build a three-dimensional geographic information system (GIS) platform for Ahmedabad, in one of the company's largest projects as it expands its digital twin and spatial intelligence business.

The project will create a city-wide digital map covering about 625 sq km and is expected to digitally capture land parcels, properties, roads and civic infrastructure, including water supply, sewerage and stormwater drainage networks, Genesys said in a statement on Thursday.
Around 2.5 million properties will be surveyed, geocoded and assigned unique digital identities as part of the project, creating a property-level spatial database for the city.
The contract will be executed over two-and-a-half years, followed by five years of operations and maintenance, the company said.

"This project is not simply about a digital map; it is about building a high-precision digital representation of the city that brings together land, properties, roads, utilities and underground infrastructure on a common spatially intelligent platform," Genesys Chairman and Managing Director Sajid Malik said.
The project will use aerial and other surveying technologies to build an elevation model of Ahmedabad, supported by 40 primary and 200 secondary survey control points, according to the company.

Genesys will also map underground infrastructure, including existing water, sewerage, stormwater drainage and cable networks, along with information on their location and depth. The data will be integrated into a central GIS database that can be accessed by municipal departments.

The company said the platform is intended to provide a common spatial reference for urban planning, infrastructure management and civic services, potentially allowing authorities to coordinate projects and manage assets using a shared digital representation of the city.

The Ahmedabad contract comes as Genesys seeks to expand beyond conventional GIS mapping into 3D digital twins, high-definition mapping and applications involving artificial intelligence and spatial data.

The company has been building three-dimensional representations of Indian cities and infrastructure by combining surveying, mapping, GIS and artificial intelligence technologies. Such systems can be used for applications including utility management, property administration, mobility planning and disaster preparedness, although the specific applications under the Ahmedabad contract will depend on how municipal authorities deploy the platform.

Malik described the project as a step towards what he called "spatial intelligence" for Indian cities, with continuously updated geospatial data being used to support government planning and infrastructure management.

Genesys said the Ahmedabad project would bring together property-level geocoding, 3D modelling and above- and below-ground infrastructure mapping on a single platform, creating a digital foundation for the city's future urban development.
